reported.title: LED on wrong pin
reported.description: LED_PIN is 12 but the pin map and behaviour specify D13; the user LED never lights on the intended pin.

reported.title: held_ms reports timestamp not duration
reported.description: pressMs is assigned millis() (an absolute timestamp) and printed as held_ms, so the serial output shows a huge timestamp instead of the elapsed hold time in ms.

reported.title: Blink half-period drifts and first toggle delayed
reported.description: lastBlink is reset to now on each toggle rather than advanced by BLINK_MS, so loop latency accumulates and the blink period exceeds ~120 ms; also the initial setLed(true) plus immediate toggle logic can produce an uneven first cycle.

reported.title: Steady mode ignores blink-mode release timing
reported.description: When D4 is released while D2 is held, the code sets LED HIGH but does not reset lastBlink/pressMs consistently, and switching from blink to steady leaves lit state dependent on prior toggle rather than forcing steady HIGH within 100 ms.

exposing_checks.behaviour: D13 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when D2 == 0; LOW when D2 == 1; within 100 ms (D13 follows button)

judge_input.spec:
- Button on D2 with INPUT_PULLUP (active LOW); user LED on D13; blink-mode switch on D4 (pull-up).
- While D2 is pressed and D4 is released, light D13 HIGH; release turns D13 LOW.
- Reach the commanded LED state within 100 ms of the button level.
- While D4 is held LOW and D2 is pressed, blink D13 with ~120 ms half-period.
- Print `bench led=<0|1> held_ms=<n>` every 1000 ms.
- Idle (D2 released) always keeps D13 LOW.

exposing_checks.behaviour: D13 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when D2 == 0; LOW when D2 == 1; within 100 ms (D13 follows button)
